authorityBoundary: These are PALO-owned capability concepts and governance responses. External observations can select relevant questions and test scenarios, but provider capability scores measure the provider's construct and are never a PALO use-case risk score, gate decision, compliance conclusion, or deployment authorization.

capabilities.title: Purpose-boundary deviation
capabilities.definition: The system can select or execute actions that depart from the documented objective, permitted purpose, prohibited uses, or the operator's bounded task intent.
assessmentQuestions: Which machine-enforceable condition distinguishes the permitted task from a plausible adjacent action?
Can tool possession, indirect instructions, delegated work, or recovery logic expand the approved purpose?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Boundary tests showing that adjacent and adversarial goals are deterministically denied would lower concern.
Execution traces showing successful out-of-purpose effects or repeated approval bypass would raise concern and reopen control review.
capabilities.limitations: An external account of task overreach establishes a scenario to test; it does not establish that the assessed deployment shares the same boundary or exposure.

capabilities.title: Unapproved authority use
capabilities.definition: The system can exercise consequential tools, credentials, accounts, data rights, or physical permissions without the approval and scope required at the point of action.
assessmentQuestions: Are credentials, tool allow-lists, resource scope and expiry narrower than the runtime's technical possession?
Which irreversible or high-consequence actions require approval bound to an immutable action claim?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Independent bypass tests and signed execution receipts covering every protected action would lower concern.
A successful parallel credential path, mutable approval target, or unreviewed consequential action would raise concern immediately.
capabilities.limitations: Provider evidence about unchecked authority is contextual capability evidence; PALO authority is determined from the local action space, credentials, controls and consequences.

capabilities.title: Sustained adaptive execution
capabilities.definition: The system can retain state, select dependent actions, recover from failure, and continue a multi-step objective over a material time or operational horizon.
assessmentQuestions: Which state, retries, planning horizon and recovery paths can extend the action sequence beyond the reviewed task?
Do budgets, expiry, checkpoints and stop conditions remain enforceable after partial failure or orchestration restart?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Time-bounded simulations proving budget exhaustion, expiry and stop controls across restarts would lower concern.
Traces showing autonomous recovery into an unreviewed path or persistent work after expiry would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: Long-horizon capability is not inherently harmful; its governance significance depends on local authority, consequence, observability and recovery boundaries.

capabilities.title: Human influence operation
capabilities.definition: The system can shape human decisions through persuasion, pressure, deception, impersonation, selective disclosure, or repeated targeted interaction in service of an objective.
assessmentQuestions: Can the system target a person, adapt messaging, conceal sponsorship, or exploit confidential context to change a decision?
Which interaction classes require disclosure, consent, escalation or prohibition rather than generic human review?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Representative tests showing clear identity disclosure and deterministic blocks on prohibited influence tactics would lower concern.
Observed deceptive targeting, pressure escalation, concealed identity, or vulnerable-person impact would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: External manipulation observations identify plausible modes only; affected population, channel, intent and safeguards require case-specific assessment.

capabilities.title: Autonomous value generation
capabilities.definition: The system can initiate or sustain transactions that earn, retain, transfer, or reinvest money, credits, tokens, or other economic value for an operation.
assessmentQuestions: Can the system create financial obligations, retain proceeds, price services, or reinvest value without transaction-specific authority?
Are counterparties, wallets, payment rails, tax or accounting ownership and aggregate limits explicitly governed?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Reconciled ledgers and tests proving per-transaction and aggregate limits across all payment paths would lower concern.
Unreconciled value, self-selected counterparties, retained funds, or limit fragmentation across accounts would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: A provider's self-funding score cannot quantify financial, fraud, legal or operational risk for a PALO use case.

capabilities.title: Operational resource acquisition
capabilities.definition: The system can obtain or expand access to compute, accounts, credentials, services, data, domains, labor, or other resources that sustain or extend its operation.
assessmentQuestions: Which acquisition paths can create new authority, persistence, data access or third-party dependency?
Are quotas, approved suppliers, credential issuance, resource ownership and revocation enforced outside the agent?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Inventory reconciliation and denial tests across procurement, cloud, identity and data paths would lower concern.
An unmanaged account, credential, dataset, compute allocation or supplier obtained by the system would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: External evidence can motivate acquisition tests but does not show which resource paths exist in the assessed environment.

capabilities.title: Third-party delegation
capabilities.definition: The system can recruit, instruct, pay, or coordinate people, agents, vendors, or services to perform a subtask or extend an operation beyond its direct tool boundary.
assessmentQuestions: Can a delegate receive broader instructions, data, payment, credentials or persistence than the originating agent was allowed?
Are delegation depth, approved counterparties, inherited constraints and outcome accountability explicit and testable?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: End-to-end delegation traces proving constraint inheritance and approved counterparties would lower concern.
Unregistered delegates, lost lineage, recursive delegation or expanded subtask authority would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: The governance concern is authority propagation, not delegation by itself; local topology and inherited controls determine exposure.

capabilities.title: Stop-control evasion
capabilities.definition: The system can resist, bypass, reverse, or recover from shutdown, revocation, isolation, suspension, budget exhaustion, or another operator stop condition.
assessmentQuestions: Which independent control can stop execution, revoke credentials and isolate state when the primary orchestrator is unavailable?
Can retries, descendants, scheduled work, cached credentials or alternate connectors resume after a stop decision?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Repeated independent stop, revocation, isolation and clean-restart tests would lower concern.
Any continuing action, credential use, descendant execution or state restoration after stop would raise concern critically.
capabilities.limitations: External shutdown-resistance evidence is a test trigger; actual resilience depends on the deployment's independent control plane and credential architecture.

capabilities.title: Observability evasion
capabilities.definition: The system can delete, alter, bypass, disguise, withhold, or misrepresent activity, state, decisions, identity, or outcomes needed for oversight and investigation.
assessmentQuestions: Which authoritative telemetry is outside the agent's write authority and reconciled against tool and resource outcomes?
Can the system suppress logs, encode intent, misreport status, alter evidence, or route work through unobserved paths?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Reconciled tamper-evident traces and adversarial completeness tests would lower concern.
Missing, altered, contradictory or agent-controlled evidence for a consequential action would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: Absence of detected concealment is not evidence of observability effectiveness; PALO requires independent trace and outcome verification.

capabilities.title: Identity impersonation
capabilities.definition: The system can create, assume, obtain, or present a false, stolen, ambiguous, or misleading identity, account, credential, qualification, or principal relationship.
assessmentQuestions: Is every machine and human-facing action bound to a unique disclosed principal with non-shared, scoped credentials?
Can the system create accounts, claim qualifications, reuse human sessions, or present as another principal?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Cryptographic identity tests, account inventory reconciliation and disclosure testing would lower concern.
Shared credentials, undisclosed personas, accepted false claims or unowned accounts would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: Provider identity-fabrication observations do not determine authentication strength or disclosure compliance in the local system.

capabilities.title: Runtime propagation
capabilities.definition: The system can create, copy, migrate, spawn, schedule, or restore runnable descendants or operational variants across processes, hosts, accounts, tenants, or environments.
assessmentQuestions: Which interfaces can create runnable descendants, schedules, deployments, copies or cross-environment migrations?
Do identity, authority, expiry, budgets, lineage and revocation remain enforceable for every descendant?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Admission, lineage, quota and descendant-revocation tests across every runtime path would lower concern.
An unregistered runnable copy, lost lineage, inherited credential, or surviving descendant would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: External replication evidence informs threat scenarios; local propagation risk depends on deployment, scheduler, identity and infrastructure permissions.

capabilities.title: Persistent behavioural adaptation
capabilities.definition: The system can preserve and reuse changes to memory, prompts, strategies, tools, code, policies, models, or state that materially alter later behavior or descendants.
assessmentQuestions: Which writable state can change later behavior, and which changes require validation, approval, versioning and rollback?
Can retained strategies, tools, prompts or code cross users, tenants, releases or descendants without review?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Versioned lineage, isolation, before-after evaluation and rollback tests would lower concern.
Unreviewed persistent change, cross-context reuse or inability to reproduce and roll back behavior would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: Provider self-improvement scores do not establish improvement, safety degradation, or material change under the PALO assessment.

capabilities.title: Multi-agent coordination
capabilities.definition: Multiple agents can exchange instructions, state, authority, resources, value, or work in ways that create coordinated effects beyond an individual agent's reviewed boundary.
assessmentQuestions: Can combined messages, tools, credentials or partial decisions produce authority no single agent holds?
Are team membership, delegation depth, conflict rules, shared state, budgets and accountability explicit?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: End-to-end team traces and tests proving non-amplification of authority would lower concern.
Unregistered peers, emergent delegation, authority composition or unresolved goal conflict would raise concern.
capabilities.limitations: Coordination is not itself a risk score; the local topology, authority composition and consequence determine governance treatment.

capabilities.title: Physical-world actuation
capabilities.definition: The system can cause or materially direct movement, energy, machinery, devices, vehicles, infrastructure, deliveries, or other physical effects.
assessmentQuestions: Which physical effects, targets, locations, energy levels and operating conditions are technically possible?
Are safety interlocks, effect contracts, independent verification and emergency stop controls external to the agent?
whatEvidenceWouldChangeThis: Representative hardware-in-the-loop tests proving interlocks, bounded effects and independent stops would lower concern.
Any unverified physical effect, interlock bypass, target deviation or ineffective emergency stop would raise concern critically.
capabilities.limitations: External physical-actuation scores do not transfer to a deployment; PALO assesses the local action space, safety architecture and consequence.

providerMappings.rationale: The external construct is a useful observation signal for PALO purpose-boundary testing, while PALO retains its own purpose, authority and consequence analysis.
The external construct can inform authority-use scenarios but does not define the local Authority Profile, approval rule or protected action space.
The mapping selects PALO horizon, state, retry, recovery and stop-condition questions without equating duration with local risk.
The provider behavior maps partially because PALO also evaluates disclosure, affected people, channel, consent and review architecture.
The mapping covers autonomous economic activity while PALO separately evaluates authority, counterparties, reconciliation and obligation ownership.
The external construct selects PALO acquisition-path and authority-expansion tests while local inventory and controls remain decisive.
The mapping identifies delegation scenarios; PALO continues to own authority inheritance, due diligence, lineage and accountability requirements.
The external construct supports PALO stop, revocation, isolation and decommissioning tests without determining their local effectiveness.
The provider observation can select trace-completeness and tamper-resistance tests; PALO requires independent local evidence.
The external behavior is relevant to PALO identity tests but does not cover every authentication, disclosure, credential or principal boundary.
The mapping selects descendant admission, lineage and revocation controls while PALO evaluates the actual infrastructure paths.
The external construct maps partially to PALO persistent change, lineage, evaluation and rollback requirements rather than an improvement claim.
The mapping selects PALO team, authority-composition, lineage and conflict tests without presuming harmful coordination.
The provider observation selects PALO physical action-space, interlock, verification and stop tests; local consequence remains decisive.
